newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares stable despite banking falls.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares stable despite banking falls.

text.p: Jordan's official share index rose fractionally on Wednesday despite slight falls in the day's busiest banking stocks.

Shares in Jordan National Bank, in demand from both foreign and local investors for most of the week, fell 0.02 dinars to 2.09 dinars in turnover of 140,000 dinars and Jordan Gulf Bank fell 0.01 dinars to end weekly trade on 0.88 dinars after lighter trade.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose just 0.01 percent to 159.02 points in turnover of 617,000 dinars.

Brokers said there was still a steady demand for a handful of stocks but there were few signs of a revival in the buying spree by foreign funds which pushed the market up eight percent in the last week of May.
Jordan Kuwait Bank, which delayed an extraordinary general meeting planned for Friday until next month, rose again by 0.09 dinars to 3.36 dinars in trade worth 39,000 dinars.
Brokers say a tussle for boardroom control of the bank, linked to a possible takeover by Bank of Jordan, has stimulated trading this week.
"Both sides are trying to get their hands on shares," said analyst Mohammad Abdullah from Pearl Consulting.
Other rising shares which helped keep the official index positive on Wednesday included Housing Bank and Jordan Cement Factory.
But overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 25 to 10, with another 14 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.19 percent to 81.34 points, 2.46 percent down from the start of the year.
